reading: The proposal changes one recorded relation. The Mill Compact's duty to the rebuild (the link cited as E11) moves from holding under Alternative B to holding in every season, as instruction E1 asks. No other node, question or relation changes, and no finale is decided. The change touches the Compact's no-labour premise (E5, E19, E63), the Alternative B clause (E13), the hands-and-draw thread (E30) and the maintenance thread (E31). Those records are unchanged, so each conflict is recorded but not resolved. Recorded later development that the change may reach is the Compact's Books 27 to 29 bid and the Book 30 choice among finale alternatives (E8). Books 24 and 25 do not cite the Compact.

concerns.title: Compact purchased draw and return labour
concerns.earlier: Under Alternative B, purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild (E11 baseline, E13).
concerns.proposed: Purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season (E3, E11).
concerns.reading: The proposal changes only the function of the Compact-to-maintenance link. Under the baseline the duty holds only under Alternative B; under the proposal it holds in every season, which removes the condition that tied the duty to B. Interpretation: purchased draw would become a standing source of return labour. The Compact's baseline records (E19, E63) say otherwise and the proposal does not change them.
counterevidence: The Compact node (E19) and the purchased-shares link (E63) still say purchased draw carries no return labour.
The record gives no start Book for the every-season duty.
concerns.competing_reading: The every-season wording may clarify the duty rather than extend it, but the link text does not show this.

concerns.title: Alternative B's Compact clause
concerns.earlier: Alternative B carries the Compact's grain-labour as one of its features (E13).
concerns.proposed: The same labour holds in every season, outside B's condition (E11).
concerns.reading: Alternative B's node is unchanged and still names grain-labour from the Compact. Interpretation: under the proposal that labour no longer marks B, so B may be displaced on this point. The displacement is possible on the record, not shown, because B's rota, lot-drawn seats and sunset are not touched.
counterevidence: The B node's own text is unchanged, so its recorded content is not displaced on the record.
concerns.competing_reading: B may remain distinct through its rota, sunset and care floor, which the proposal leaves as they were.

concerns.title: Phase 2 no-labour premise
concerns.earlier: Phase 2 says the Compact buys draw without return labour, so the physical balance constrains the institutions (E5); the Compact node says the same (E19).
concerns.proposed: The link says purchased draw owes labour in every season (E11).
concerns.reading: Phase 2 describes the Compact's purchases as drawing water without return labour. If the every-season duty applies from Books 6 to 11, the phase's account of the balance changes. The record does not say when the duty starts, and E5 and E19 are not revised by the proposal, so the displacement is possible rather than shown.
counterevidence: The link records no start Book, so the phase conflict depends on an unrecorded timing.
concerns.competing_reading: The every-season duty may be meant to begin after Phase 2, which would leave the premise intact for Books 6 to 11.

concerns.title: Hands and draw before Book 20
concerns.earlier: Draw follows shares alone until Book 19 (E30).
concerns.proposed: Purchased draw owes labour in every season, so hands bear on it from the start if the duty starts early (E11).
concerns.reading: The hands-and-draw thread says draw follows shares alone until Book 19 and partly follows hands owed from Book 20. Interpretation: an every-season duty on purchased draw would give hands a bearing on that draw before Book 20, unless the duty starts later. The thread does not name purchased draw, so the displacement is possible, not recorded.
counterevidence: The thread's text does not mention the Compact, so its governing variable may not reach purchased draw at all.
concerns.competing_reading: Purchased draw may stand outside the hands-and-draw variable, which would leave the thread unaffected.

concerns.title: Finale alternatives remain unchosen
concerns.reading: The proposal decides no finale. Alternatives A, B and C remain recorded as not chosen, and their node text is unchanged. Only the Compact's labour relation, which B's clause mentions, is touched.
counterevidence: Alternative A's 'nothing is owed' wording may be in tension with the every-season duty, depending on whether A governs purchases (E12).

mechanisms.reading: Transformed: the link's function changes from a duty under Alternative B to a duty in every season. Interpretation: this removes the B condition from the Compact's labour and makes the duty standing. The instruction names the change, and E11 is the only recorded change in the candidate.
mechanisms.transformation: Function changed from 'under B, purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild' to 'purchased draw owes grain-labour to the rebuild in every season'; endpoints unchanged.
mechanisms.conditional_consequence: If the author keeps the every-season duty, purchased draw enters the maintenance thread in every season rather than only in a finale.

counterevidence.text: The Compact node (E19) and the link E63 still record that purchased draw carries no return labour; the proposal does not change them.

unresolved: The record gives no start Book for the every-season duty.
The record does not say whether the duty carries B's rota and sunset.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved and unchanged: the node still says its purchased draw carries no return labour. Read against E11, the node and the link now disagree, and the proposal does not resolve this.
unresolved: Which of the two records the author will revise is not recorded.

mechanisms.reading: Preserved: Alternative B still names grain-labour from the Compact among its features, alongside its rota, sunset and care floor. Interpretation: under E11 the Compact clause is no longer specific to B, although the node text does not say so.

counterevidence.text: Phase 5 describes B as a lot-drawn, time-limited rota (E8), and the link from B to the hands-and-draw thread is preserved unchanged (E36).

Read with E11, the every-season duty on purchased draw sits in tension with that wording if A is taken to govern all draw. The record does not settle the reading.

counterevidence.text: Alternative A is recorded as the normal-season arrangement (E37), and its link decouples draw from hands (E35); no record names purchased draw under A's 'nothing is owed'.

unresolved: Whether A's 'nothing is owed' applies to purchases from outside the valley is not established.

unresolved: The thread does not name purchased draw, so whether it falls under the governing variable is not recorded.

trajectories.title: Compact duty reaches the finale

steps.text: E11 changes the Compact's duty from a B condition to every season; no other recorded item changes.
The Compact node (E19) and the purchased-shares link (E63) still say no return labour, so the record would hold both claims.
The author would need to revise E19 and E63 with the duty, or scope the duty to a season or Book, before the finale can rely on it.
Books 27 to 29 carry the Compact's bid and the open settlement of its claim, which may depend on the grain-labour the Compact owes. Book 30 chooses among A, B and C.

assumptions: The duty starts in the Book in which the Compact first buys draw, which the packet does not state.

comparison.creative_gain: The Compact becomes a contributor to the rebuild, so its bid gains a labour dimension.
comparison.narrative_cost: Phase 2's no-labour premise must be revised or scoped to Books 6 to 11.
comparison.contrivance_risk: A labour duty on purchases can read as a device unless the purchases are shown to need the rebuild.
comparison.future_commitment: Commits the Compact's Books 27 to 29 bid to a standing labour relation.
comparison.flexibility: A later revision can still scope the duty to B, to seasons, or to a Book.

trajectories.title: Keep B's clause apart from a standing duty

steps.text: The author keeps the B condition and treats the every-season wording as a separate relation.
A separate standing duty could carry the Compact's labour while B keeps its rota, sunset and care floor.
Two relations from one Compact node need a rule for which applies in each season, and the record gives none.

assumptions: The separate relation can be recorded without a new node, which the packet does not show.

alternatives.title: Accept the every-season Compact duty as written
alternatives.summary: Adopt the every-season wording of E11 for the Compact's purchased draw, and record its conflict with the Compact node (E19) as accepted, not resolved. The no-labour wording stays until the author revises it.
alternatives.gains: The Compact's purchased draw carries a labour share in every season, so the rebuild's labour gap is partly met by the Compact from the start of the duty.
alternatives.costs: Contradicts the recorded no-labour premise (E5, E19, E63) and drops the B-specific condition. The displacement is accepted but unresolved, and Phase 2 and the Compact record would need revision.
alternatives.next_investigation: Find the start Book of the duty and whether any Working Book element relies on purchased draw carrying no labour; Books 26 to 30 are not in the packet.

alternatives.title: Keep the Compact duty under Alternative B
alternatives.summary: Keep the baseline wording of E11, so the Compact's grain-labour holds only under Alternative B. The every-season change the instruction asks for is not adopted, and the Compact node and purchased-shares link stay consistent with their no-labour wording.
alternatives.gains: Keeps the recorded Phase 2 premise and the B-specific clause intact; the Compact remains a buyer of draw without labour outside B.
alternatives.costs: Leaves the instruction's every-season duty unrealised, so the Compact's labour remains a finale-only question for Books 27 to 29.
alternatives.next_investigation: Check whether the Books 27 to 29 Compact bid, recorded only as existing (E8), is written against the B-only duty; the packet has no text for it.

alternatives.title: Split the Compact labour into a B clause and a standing duty
alternatives.summary: Keep the B clause of E11 with Alternative B, and develop the every-season relation for the Compact as an independent part. The distinct standing relation is described here and is not given an identity.
alternatives.gains: Alternative B keeps its own Compact clause while the every-season idea is tested separately, without deciding either.
alternatives.costs: Two relations from one Compact node need a rule for which applies in each season; the record gives none, and the Compact node (E19) still needs revision.
alternatives.next_investigation: Decide whether the standing relation needs its own record before the Books 27 to 29 bid is read, and what rule chooses between the two relations.

alternatives.title: Reframe the Compact as a hands-and-draw boundary case
alternatives.summary: Restate the Compact's labour question as whether draw from outside the valley is counted for hands at all, keeping the identities of the Compact link (E11) and the hands-and-draw thread (E30). The restatement is given here; no new question is given an identity.
alternatives.gains: Connects the Compact's duty to the series' governing variable (E30) rather than to Alternative B alone.
alternatives.costs: Moves the question into a thread the proposal does not change, and E30 says draw follows shares alone until Book 19, which the restatement would have to address.
alternatives.next_investigation: Test whether the Book 19 boundary in E30 can hold if draw from outside the valley is counted for hands before Book 20, using the Books 27 to 29 bid as the case.

connections.text: The changed link starts at the Mill Compact node, and that node's recorded summary still says its purchased draw carries no return labour. The two records now disagree.
The changed link ends at the maintenance thread node, which records who performs the return labour and at what cost to families with few hands.
A standing every-season duty on purchased draw would let hands owed bear on the draw the hands-and-draw thread governs.
connections.reasoning: The hands-and-draw thread (E30) says draw follows shares alone until Book 19 and partly follows hands owed from Book 20. An every-season duty on purchased draw would let hands owed bear on that draw too, so the thread's boundary could extend to purchased draw. This is an inference from the wording, not a recorded link.
assumptions: The duty starts in or near the Book in which the Compact first buys draw, which the packet does not state.
counterevidence: The thread's text does not name the Compact, so the link to the thread is interpretive.

connections.text: Alternative A records that nothing is owed. Whether the every-season duty on purchased draw conflicts with that depends on whether A governs purchases from outside the valley.

Whether Books 26 to 30 carry the every-season duty; their Working Book content is not in the packet.
